question: Does the BMB 2014 Atlas provide a historical Central Luzon inland-water crosswalk for the RDP's reported 168 wetland units, and what does the source establish about the count, names and river scope?

sourceDocuments.title: Atlas of Inland Wetlands in Mainland Luzon, Philippines
sourceDocuments.publisher: Biodiversity Management Bureau, Department of Environment and Natural Resources
reviewedSections: Table 1, all Region III rows: codes 53-66 and 105
Map 1 river-system count table and its notes
Table 2 selected Region III watercourse rows for Angat, Pantabangan, Pampanga, and shared-boundary crosswalks
sourceDocuments.accessNote: PDF text and table rows reviewed through the browser's extracted PDF text. The Ramsar host returned HTTP 403 to a direct local fetch; no local PDF or table image is retained.

sourceDocuments.title: Central Luzon Regional Development Plan 2023-2028
sourceDocuments.publisher: Department of Economy, Planning, and Development Region III
reviewedSections: Wetlands and River Systems section, official PDF text returned in web search
sourceDocuments.accessNote: The official PDF search result exposes the relevant text; the direct PDF request previously returned HTTP 403. No local PDF is retained.

rdpReported.separateRiverStatement: The RDP also states that Central Luzon has 202 rivers. Its definition and relationship to the 153 major/minor rivers counted among the 168 wetlands are not provided in the reviewed passage.

sourceNotes: Map 1 says a single asterisk marks a river system draining toward the same stream that was counted as one unit.
Map 1 says double asterisks identify the province where a river system is counted.
The markers are retained verbatim in selected Table 2 names; this review does not infer row-level meanings for triple- or quadruple-marker forms.

countCrosswalk.finding: The BMB Atlas independently reports the same 153 river-system subtotal and a matching 11-lake, 3-water-storage-area, 1-swamp Table 1 breakdown, yielding 168 named-category units at the count level. This is an exact arithmetic and category-level concordance with the RDP statement, not proof that both publications use the same source, definitions, date, or exact set of waterbodies.
countCrosswalk.decision: Count-level crosswalk supported; the named waterbody denominator remains incomplete and the underlying unit/source lineage remains unresolved. Do not label the RDP's 168 a verified current inventory.

method.table1Selection: Every Table 1 row explicitly assigned to Region III: codes 53-66 and 105. Area values are preserved as the atlas's approximate historical hectares.
method.table2Selection: A non-exhaustive subset selected for explicit named connections to Angat Reservoir, Pantabangan Reservoir and Pampanga River, plus cross-region/shared-province rows visible in those table sections. This is not a transcription of all Region III river systems.

limitations: The exact count/category match does not establish that the 2023-2028 RDP derived its numbers from the 2014 Atlas or that both sources define units identically.
The RDP's separate statement of 202 rivers is not reconciled with the 153 river systems counted in its 168-unit wetland breakdown or the Atlas map table.
The Table 1 list is complete only for rows the 2014 Atlas assigns to Region III; it is not a current or exhaustive inventory of rivers, streams, tributaries, wetlands, ponds or aquatic habitats.
Only 20 selected Table 2 rows were transcribed. Names, map grids and outflows do not establish exact channel identity, basin boundary, route geometry, waterbody boundary or current status.
The Atlas describes its inland-wetland locations and boundaries as requiring ground verification and survey/delineation; administrative boundaries are approximate.

The source is historical and does not establish fish identity, present fish presence or absence, catchability, access, fishing rules, water quality, hazard status, diet, safety, or species-specific photo references.

The Atlas copyright page permits reproduction for educational or non-profit purposes with acknowledgement; this is not a general open-data license. No public-app redistribution or derived-database rights are approved by this review.
nextStep: Resolve the RDP's 202 rivers statement and source lineage for its 168-unit category count, transcribe or locate a current complete name-level L3 waterbody source, then independently crosswalk atlas names to current hydrology/admin units and seek dated, taxon-resolved, reusable fish evidence for each waterbody. Keep the Central Luzon baseline incomplete.
